body.statement: At every \(q_\star\) satisfying the equivalent conditions of the continuity frontier on a specified sampling face \(E\), does the projected full-loss germ handle consistently recover all and only the zero-intercept homogeneous pieces of \(f(q_\star+v,q_\star)\) on every feasible \(v\in T\), including continuous multi-path switches and propensity--grid ties, so that \[\sqrt n\,d_H(S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star))\Rightarrow\psi_{q_\star}(G)\] and Gaussian simulation of the recovered germ gives pointwise asymptotically valid Hausdorff balls?
body.justification: This is the nonroutine inference step: path labels alone do not determine the active Hausdorff-loss pieces.
body.gap: Fang--Santos presumes access to a consistently estimable directional map, while Kaido--Molinari--Stoye treats smooth projections rather than law-dependent unions on relative faces.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields root-\(n\) calibrated metric inference at certified regular Oregon-type laws without claiming global regularity.
